objects.description: Internal state and buffers for the cava audio visualization core. Applications receive a pointer to this plan from cava_init, pass it to cava_execute for processing, and finally to cava_destroy for cleanup. Fields include FFTW plans and buffers, configuration (number of bars, channels, rate), sensitivity/noise reduction parameters, cutoff-related data, and status/error reporting. The comments advise users not to modify fields directly; treat as opaque outside of cavacore.

functions.name: cava_init
functions.signature: struct cava_plan *cava_init(int number_of_bars, unsigned int rate, int channels, int autosens, double noise_reduction, int low_cut_off, int high_cut_off);
functions.description: Initializes the cavacore visualization engine and returns an allocated cava_plan describing the processing plan. Use this before calling cava_execute. The plan carries configuration such as bar count, sample rate, channels, sensitivity, noise reduction, and frequency cutoffs; its status field indicates success or failure and error_message contains details on invalid parameters.
requirements: Caller must pass the desired number_of_bars per channel (unspecified minimum/maximum; illegal values cause plan->status == -1).
rate must be a valid audio sample rate in Hz (unsigned integer; e.g., > 0).
channels is the number of interleaved input channels; only up to two channels are supported by cavacore.
autosens is a toggle: 1 to enable automatic sensitivity (output dynamically scaled to 0..1), 0 to disable (raw values).
noise_reduction is a smoothing factor in the range [0.0, 1.0]; recommended value: 0.77.
low_cut_off and high_cut_off are cutoff frequencies for visualization in Hz; recommended values: 50 and 10000.
On return, caller must check plan != NULL and plan->status: 0 indicates success; -1 indicates an illegal parameter (details in plan->error_message).
Caller is responsible for eventually freeing the plan via cava_destroy when finished.

functions.name: cava_execute
functions.signature: void cava_execute(double *cava_in, int new_samples, double *cava_out, struct cava_plan *plan);
functions.description: Processes input audio samples and produces a bar-spectrum visualization output according to the provided cava_plan. Accepts interleaved input for multi-channel audio and writes bars sorted from lowest to highest frequency; for stereo, all left-channel bars precede right-channel bars.
requirements: plan must be a valid pointer to a cava_plan previously returned by cava_init with plan->status == 0.
cava_in must point to at least new_samples samples of input, interleaved if channels > 1.
Only up to two input channels are supported; if more than one channel, input must be interleaved.
new_samples is the number of samples to process this call; it may vary between calls.
If new_samples exceeds cavacore's internal buffer capacity (4096 * number_of_channels at 44100 Hz), excess samples will be discarded.
cava_out must point to a buffer sized for (number_of_bars * number_of_channels) doubles; bars are ordered low-to-high frequency, and for stereo all left bars come before right bars.
Using smaller new_samples increases output frame rate (e.g., 512 samples at 44100 Hz mono yields ~86 FPS).
All pointers passed (cava_in, cava_out, plan) must be non-null and valid for reading/writing as appropriate.

functions.name: cava_destroy
functions.description: Releases resources associated with a cava_plan created by cava_init. Call this when visualization is no longer needed.
requirements: plan must be a cava_plan previously returned by cava_init.
After calling, the plan is invalid and must not be used again (including in cava_execute).
Caller should avoid calling cava_destroy more than once on the same plan pointer (double-free behavior is unspecified).

endpoints.name: cava_init
cava_execute
cava_destroy

data_types.description: Arbitrary byte sequence interpreted as IEEE-754 double-precision values when copied into a double buffer. The bytes are not expected to be valid text or any structured format; they are consumed cyclically to populate an array of doubles representing interleaved audio samples for 1–2 channels.

generators.generator:
import random
import struct
from typing import List

# This generator produces raw bytes that will be cyclically memcpy'd into doubles
# in the fuzzer stub to form interleaved audio samples (1-2 channels). We focus on
# creating byte patterns that map to interesting IEEE-754 double values when read
# little-endian or big-endian, including:
# - canonical small/large magnitudes
# - exact integers, powers of two
# - denormals/subnormals
# - signed zeros
# - infinities and NaNs (quiet/signaling patterns)
# - alternating patterns to exercise stereo interleaving
# The stub cycles the bytes, so we keep the set diverse and short (< 4096 bytes).

# Helper: pack u64 to bytes little-endian
_def_le = lambda u: struct.pack('<Q', u & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF)
_def_be = lambda u: struct.pack('>Q', u & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF)

# Predefined interesting bit patterns for doubles
INTERESTING_U64 = [
    0x0000000000000000,  # +0.0
    0x8000000000000000,  # -0.0
    0x3FF0000000000000,  # 1.0
    0xBFF0000000000000,  # -1.0
    0x4000000000000000,  # 2.0
    0xC000000000000000,  # -2.0
    0x4024000000000000,  # 10.0
    0xC024000000000000,  # -10.0
    0x7FF0000000000000,  # +inf
    0xFFF0000000000000,  # -inf
    0x7FF8000000000000,  # qNaN
    0x7FF0000000000001,  # sNaN-ish (impl-defined)
    0x0000000000000001,  # smallest subnormal
    0x8000000000000001,  # negative subnormal
    0x0010000000000000,  # smallest normal
    0x7FEFFFFFFFFFFFFF,  # max finite
    0xFFEFFFFFFFFFFFFF,  # -max finite
    0x3FE0000000000000,  # 0.5
    0xBFE0000000000000,  # -0.5
    0x3FB999999999999A,  # 0.1
    0xBFB999999999999A,  # -0.1
    0x3FD3333333333333,  # 0.3
    0x3FF199999999999A,  # 1.1
    0x402921FB54442D18,  # pi
    0xC00921FB54442D18,  # -pi*2
]

def _make_stereo_pattern(a_le: bytes, b_le: bytes) -> bytes:
    # Interleave two 8-byte sequences to mimic alternating channel-heavy input
    # The stub cycles bytes per double, not per channel, but alternating patterns
    # introduce variety across consecutive doubles.
    return a_le + b_le

def _random_double_bytes(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    choice = rng.randrange(0, 6)
    if choice == 0:
        # Random normal range via uniform exponent/mantissa
        sign = rng.getrandbits(1)
        exp = rng.randrange(1, 2046)
        mant = rng.getrandbits(52)
        u = (sign << 63) | (exp << 52) | mant
        return _def_le(u)
    if choice == 1:
        # Subnormal
        sign = rng.getrandbits(1)
        mant = rng.randrange(1, 1 << 52)
        u = (sign << 63) | mant
        return _def_le(u)
    if choice == 2:
        # Interesting constants
        u = rng.choice(INTERESTING_U64)
        # randomly flip a low bit to generate nearby representable values
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            u ^= 1 << rng.randrange(0, 6)
        return _def_le(u)
    if choice == 3:
        # Big-endian storage of interesting constant (still treated as opaque bytes)
        u = rng.choice(INTERESTING_U64)
        return _def_be(u)
    if choice == 4:
        # Short repeated byte pattern (e.g., 0x00, 0xFF, 0xAA, 0x55)
        b = rng.choice([0x00, 0xFF, 0xAA, 0x55, 0x11, 0xEE])
        return bytes([b]) * 8
    # choice == 5
    # Alternating nibbles
    b1 = rng.choice([0xF0, 0x0F, 0xCC, 0x33, 0x5A, 0xA5])
    return bytes([b1, 255 - b1] * 4)

def _assemble_palette(rng: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    pal: List[bytes] = []
    # Seed palette with canonical values (both LE and BE for diversity)
    for u in INTERESTING_U64:
        pal.append(_def_le(u))
    for u in [0x3FF8000000000000, 0x4008000000000000, 0x4014000000000000]:  # 1.5, 3.0, 5.0
        pal.append(_def_le(u))
    # Include some BE forms
    for u in [0x7FF8000000000001, 0x000FFFFFFFFFFFFF]:
        pal.append(_def_be(u))

    # Add randomized entries
    for _ in range(32):
        pal.append(_random_double_bytes(rng))

    # Create some stereo-ish sequences by concatenating two doubles
    stereo_pairs = []
    for _ in range(8):
        stereo_pairs.append(_make_stereo_pattern(_random_double_bytes(rng), _random_double_bytes(rng)))
    pal.extend(stereo_pairs)

    # Short ramps: bytes that, when cycled, produce gradually changing doubles
    for step in [1, 3, 7, 13]:
        base = rng.randrange(0, 256)
        seq = bytes(((base + i * step) & 0xFF for i in range(8)))
        pal.append(seq)

    return pal

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide total output size (the stub keeps <= 256 doubles, i.e., 2048 bytes);
    # we’ll produce between 64 and 2048 bytes to cover cycling behavior.
    total_len = rng.randrange(64, 2049)

    pal = _assemble_palette(rng)

    # Strategy: build the buffer from a mix of whole-double chunks and shorter
    # byte patterns to ensure good coverage when the stub cycles the data.
    out = bytearray()

    # Start with a header-like region of diverse doubles
    for _ in range(rng.randrange(4, 16)):
        out += rng.choice(pal)
        if len(out) >= total_len:
            break

    # Mix in varied chunk sizes to desynchronize from 8-byte boundaries
    while len(out) < total_len:
        mode = rng.randrange(0, 5)
        if mode == 0:
            # append a full double
            out += rng.choice(pal)
        elif mode == 1:
            # append two-doubles stereo pattern or random pair
            chunk = rng.choice(pal)
            if len(chunk) != 16:
                chunk = chunk + rng.choice(pal)  # ensure ~16
            out += chunk
        elif mode == 2:
            # append a slice of a pattern (1..7 bytes)
            pat = rng.choice(pal)
            start = rng.randrange(0, max(1, len(pat)))
            slen = rng.randrange(1, 8)
            piece = (pat * ((slen + len(pat) - 1) // len(pat)))[start:start + slen]
            out += piece
        elif mode == 3:
            # small repeating motif (e.g., 3- or 5-byte repeats)
            motif = rng.choice(pal)
            mlen = rng.choice([3, 5, 6, 7])
            motif = (motif * ((mlen + len(motif) - 1) // len(motif)))[:mlen]
            reps = rng.randrange(2, 10)
            out += motif * reps
        else:
            # random synthesized double bytes
            out += _random_double_bytes(rng)

        if len(out) > total_len:
            out = out[:total_len]
            break

    # Ensure non-empty and limit to 4096 bytes as required
    if not out:
        out = bytearray(_def_le(0x3FF0000000000000))  # fallback 1.0
    if len(out) > 4096:
        out = out[:4096]

    return bytes(out)
